discriminating_experiment.design: cv_overlap_resurvey_iter3.md §3-3: if id3/id1 waits vanish and wall drops ~sum(residual) -> round-trip hypothesis holds; if waits migrate to production gates and wall doesn't drop -> V-side throughput is the floor, redirect to V-side compression
discriminating_experiment.result: HYBRID — neither branch cleanly. (a) Release waits DID fall as designed: V_id3 20.43->7.51 (-63%), C_id1 33.73->13.29 (-61%), C_id5 12.27->5.00: the FIFO counting-token mechanism is empirically confirmed and the 2-slot round-trip coupling WAS loosened. (b) But wall ROSE: data-ready (production) waits inflated by more than the release-wait savings — C_id2 +43.8us, V_id0 +10.7us, V_id4 +14.7us (R3). Busy times unchanged => both sides' production LATENCY grew under unpaced operation.
discriminating_experiment.conclusion: The shipped 'pacing stall' (G1's WS1_V2C release-wait) is LOAD-BEARING: by throttling C's run-ahead to ~1 step it keeps MTE2/M/FIX hardware-queue residency shallow and the ws L2 hot-set tight (2 active slots). With 4 tokens C issues up to ~4 steps of G1 work ahead; producer/consumer streams spread over a 2x ws footprint and deep queues, so every data-ready handoff (ws_s FIX -> SM, ws_p MTE3 -> G2, ws_o FIX -> AO) lands later despite identical busy work. The iter3 steady-period model 'wall = busy + round-trip residual' is FALSIFIED: the round-trip stall overlaps useful pipe drain; removing it does not convert 1:1 into wall reduction. (Mechanism attribution queue-residency vs L2-hot-set/bandwidth is INFERENCE from wait-id shifts + busy-time invariance; no instruction-level trace, L2 metrics not collected.)

framework_findings: (NEW, load-bearing) Slot-index deepening ALONE is a semantic NO-OP for this protocol: the 6 cross semaphores are SINGLE counting ids with one set/wait per u, so the k-th wait strictly consumes the k-th set (FIFO) — gates stay pinned at SM(x)<-G2(x-1), G1(x)<-SM(x-1), G2(x)<-AO(x-1) regardless of slot count. Loosening requires raising the init pre-set tokens of the 3 release semaphores to ns_flat (fresh-slot tokens). iter3's C1 write-up ('set/wait counts unchanged' + 'gates become G2(x-4)') implicitly assumed this token change; the iter4 implementation made it explicit (C-scope init 1->4, V-scope init 1->4 x2 sems). Empirical confirmation: release waits fell 61-63% exactly as the token model predicts.

(iter3 §2.3 off-by-one, corrected) With 1 init token the effective shipped gates are SM(x)<-G2(x-1) / G1(x)<-SM(x-1) / G2(x)<-AO(x-1) — one beat TIGHTER than the slot-exact requirement (G2(x-2)/SM(x-2)/AO(x-2)) quoted in the iter3 report. iter2's own docstring ('G1(x) wait == SM(x-1) consumed') had it right.

(perf principle, measured) In this kernel family, cross-core ring DEPTH is not a free lever: the release-wait 'stall' doubles as queue-depth pacing. Any future deepening (incl. C2's ws design) must keep the shipped 1-token release gating (ns=2 semantics) unless the production-side latency inflation is separately addressed.

(data quality) PipeUtilization.csv can contain impossible single-block rows (r3_g2first_s2 block19 aic_time=1395us vs TaskDur 75.14us) — always sanity-filter per-core times against TaskDur before max/mean aggregation. TaskDur (adoption metric) unaffected.
